suggestions.quote: Day thirty-three. Forty million euros. Jonas has a football club. Not supports. Has. The one at the end of the tram line, that loses every Saturday.
suggestions.fix: Force the connector from the failed spending run: `Four million gone, and the balance still rose. Therefore, day thirty-three: Jonas has a football club. Not supports. Has.`

suggestions.quote: You call Herr Brandt. Now. The universe can wait. Berlin can't.
suggestions.fix: Restore a two-right-answers dilemma immediately before this action: `Call now, and every promise you made with that money breaks. Wait one night, and the damage doubles. You call Herr Brandt.`

suggestions.quote: Never hit zero, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven your account holds more cents than the estimated number of atoms in the observable universe (c12).
suggestions.fix: Make the scale tighten the present decision rather than merely grow: follow it with `That is what one missed midnight becomes. And Berlin has one left.`

keep.quote: Jonas: I don't know what to do with my hands when they win.
It isn't taken from anyone. Except it is. From everyone. A little. Every night.
